texts.preamble: Kailash Chandra vs State (2023:Rj-Jd:41903) on 29 November, 2023 Author: Praveer Bhatnagar Bench: Praveer Bhatnagar [2023:Rj-Jd:41903] High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 943/2004 Kailash Chandra ----Petitioner Versus State ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rajiv Bishnoi For Respondent(s) : Mr. Andaram Choudhary - Pp Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Praveer Bhatnagar Order 29/11/2023 1. By way of filing this criminal revision petition challenge has been made to the judgment dated 13.12.2004 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Sc/St (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Pratapgarh in Criminal Appeal No.31/2004, whereby the learned appellate court has affirmed the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 05.02.2004 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pratapgarh in Criminal Regular Case No.121/1997, whereby the petitioner has been convicted for the offence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to suffer one year's of simple imprisonment along with fine of Rs. 2,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo three months' simple imprisonment.
texts.arguments: 2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he will not assail conviction of the petitioner and confine his arguments to the alternative prayer of reduction of the sentence [2023:RJ-JD:41903] (2 of 3) [CRLR-943/2004] awarded by the trial court. He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1997 and the present criminal revision is pending since the year 2004. The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial. With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him. 5. This Court in view of the judicial pronouncements made by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Panchram vs The State Of Chhattisgarh and Ors. reported in AIR 2023 SC 1801 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of petitioner, his status in the society and the fact that he faced financial hardship and had to go through mental agony, is of the view that ends of justice would be met, if sentence imposed upon him is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he will not assail conviction of the petitioner and confine his arguments to the alternative prayer of reduction of the sentence [2023:RJ-JD:41903] (2 of 3) [CRLR-943/2004] awarded by the trial court. He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1997 and the present criminal revision is pending since the year 2004. The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial. With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: 5. This Court in view of the judicial pronouncements made by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Panchram vs The State Of Chhattisgarh and Ors. reported in AIR 2023 SC 1801 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of petitioner, his status in the society and the fact that he faced financial hardship and had to go through mental agony, is of the view that ends of justice would be met, if sentence imposed upon him is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
